detail.body:
Co-authors: @michael-gpu, @tomasruizt 
cc @ArcheyChen 

## Overview

Revert https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54442, which introduces a performance regression under PP + spec decode with structured outputs, and re-fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54437 by addressing the root cause in `DraftTokensHandler`.

Rework of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61348, rebased, with remaining comments addressed, pre-commit fixed, and simplified implementation + tests.

## Claims

#54442 patched the issue in #54437 by masking out the draft tokens after a handoff race in `DraftTokensHandler`. This fixes #61348 but effectively shortens the draft sequence, causing an acceptance-length (and performance) regression under PP + spec decode with structured outputs.

This PR addresses the `DraftTokensHandler` handoff race directly, fixing the original issue #54437 while maintaining acceptance length.

This PR also adds an E2E repro for #54437 and acceptance length regression.

## Validation

Correctness:

E2E repro in `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_structured_output_pp.py`, serves `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` + `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` + PP=2 and sends it a mix of constrained and unconstrained requests.

```
pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_structured_output_pp.py
```

On main, fails on `_assert_specdec_metrics`, showing a regression in acceptance rate and acceptance length
```
FAILED tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_structured_output_pp.py::test_specdec_pp_structured_output[pp2-tp1] - AssertionError: (0.056471083070452156, 0.08341)
```

After revert #54442, fails on `_assert_outputs_are_structured`, showing unconstrained sampling reported by #54437
```
FAILED tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_structured_output_pp.py::test_specdec_pp_structured_output[pp2-tp1] - AssertionError: ["blue", "
```

This branch
```
1 passed, 3 warning
```

More tests
```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output

571 passed, 2 xfailed, 58 warnings

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_draft_tokens_handler.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_i64.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model

140 passed, 3 skipped, 19 warnings
```

Performance:

https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/e15dc602fbfd11e2b64c2d41527a1a72

`Qwen/Qwen3-4B` + `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark` + 8 draft tokens + async scheduling + structured outputs.
Ran on H100 80GB.

```
.venv/bin/python run.py --output ... --pipeline-parallel-size ... --num-repeats 10
```

Results report throughput in tokens/s.
- broad vs tight constraints: less vocab masked vs more vocab masked
- c1 vs c96: low vs high concurrency
- 95% confidence intervals in brackets

No regression on PP=1

Case | Main avg [95% CI] | PR avg [95% CI] | Change
-- | -- | -- | --
broad / c1 | 673.6 [668.3, 678.9] | 675.7 [666.5, 684.9] | +0.32%
broad / c96 | 9,835.7 [9,749.2, 9,922.2] | 9,785.8 [9,690.9, 9,880.7] | −0.51%
tight / c1 | 1,057.8 [1,047.7, 1,067.9] | 1,062.4 [1,051.7, 1,073.1] | +0.43%
tight / c96 | 18,582.1 [18,469.9, 18,694.3] | 18,565.3 [18,389.4, 18,741.2] | −0.09%

</body></html>

Recover performance regression on PP=2

Case | Main avg [95% CI] | PR avg [95% CI] | Change
-- | -- | -- | --
broad / c1 | 661.45 [660.82, 662.08] | 662.79 [662.39, 663.19] | +0.20%
broad / c96 | 3,951.12 [3,822.93, 4,079.30] | 12,038.09 [11,768.25, 12,307.93] | +204.68%
tight / c1 | 1,021.45 [1,020.70, 1,022.19] | 1,024.63 [1,023.00, 1,026.26] | +0.31%
tight / c96 | 3,865.53 [3,771.94, 3,959.13] | 21,029.32 [20,574.89, 21,483.75] | +444.02%

</body></html>

## Details

### Background

`DraftTokensHandler` allows workers to asynchronously send draft tokens back to the scheduler / structured output manager for processing.

With async scheduling, it works roughly like:
```
Scheduler-side                          Worker-side
--------------------------------------------------
schedule step N
sample step N
                                        execute step N
schedule step N+1
wait for step N
                                        sample step N
                                        DraftTokensHandler.set_draft_tokens
                                        execute step N+1
DraftTokensHandler.get_draft_tokens
generate sampling bitmasks
sample step N+1
                                        sample step N+1
...
```

On main, `DraftTokensHandler` holds the latest batch set by the worker. This works fine for PP=1, but when PP>=2, this can occur:
```
Scheduler-side          Worker-side
----------------------------------
                        set_draft_tokens(micro-batch A)
                        set_draft_tokens(micro-batch B)
get_draft_tokens
```

Micro-batch B replaces micro-batch A in the handler. Scheduler-side cannot recover A's drafts and generates incorrect grammar bitmasks, leading to #54437.

#54442 fixes this by effectively truncating the worker-side draft sequence, reducing acceptance length.

This PR fixes this by making `DraftTokensHandler` track draft tokens by request ID. So micro-batch B cannot override micro-batch A.

Final notes:
- Suggest reviewing commits independently
  - `e3595db629d88881e74eafc357e471924b4d9c1f`: revert #54442, could be a separate PR
  - `c67afdec130ca06c6beb5e286a5b83b91fdae3a2`: track draft tokens by request ID.
  - `bb3694db86066ea2d272051b0495bad3ae09d026`: E2E repro
- Alternative #61348 includes adding a debug flag to catch the handoff race, this is not included in this PR in favor of the E2E repro.

+    "type": "array",
+    "minItems": 16,
+    "maxItems": 16,
+    "items": {"type": "string", "enum": ["red", "blue"]},

+def case_to_test(pp_size: int, tp_size: int) -> ArgsTest:
+    """Exercise structured draft handoffs across repeated request cohorts."""

+        target_model="Qwen/Qwen3-4B",

+        pipeline_parallel_size=pp_size,

+        max_num_seqs=8,  # force multiple PP batches
+        gpu_memory_utilization=0.8,

+            # The handoff race only exists with deferred (async) sampling.
+            "async_scheduling": True,
+            "structured_outputs_config": {
+                "backend": "xgrammar",
+                "disable_any_whitespace": True,
+            },
+        },
+    )
+
+
+@multi_gpu_only(num_gpus=2)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "args",
+    [
+        pytest.param(case_to_test(pp_size=2, tp_size=1), id="pp2-tp1"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_specdec_pp_structured_output(args: ArgsTest, vllm_runner) -> None:
+    # Alternate full-size cohorts to turn over request IDs while PP batches are
+    # still in flight.
+    messages, sampling_params = _create_requests(
+        args.sampling_config,
+        num_cycles=NUM_REQUEST_CYCLES,
+        cohort_size=args.max_num_seqs,
+    )
+    kwargs = vllm_runner_kwargs(args)
+    with vllm_runner(args.target_model, **kwargs) as runner:
+        outputs = runner.llm.chat(
+            messages,
+            sampling_params,
+            chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False},
+        )
+        metrics = runner.llm.get_metrics()
+    _assert_outputs_are_structured(outputs, sampling_params)
+    _assert_specdec_metrics(
+        metrics,
+        expected_acceptance_rate=args.expected_acceptance_rate,
+        expected_acceptance_len=args.expected_acceptance_len,
+    )
+
+
+def _create_requests(
+    sampling: SamplingParams, num_cycles: int, cohort_size: int
+) -> tuple[list, list[SamplingParams]]:
+    messages = []
+    sampling_params: list[SamplingParams] = []
+    request_index = 0
+    for _ in range(num_cycles):
+        for is_structured in (True, False):
+            for _ in range(cohort_size):
+                messages.append(_make_messages(request_index, is_structured))
+                params = sampling.clone()
+                if is_structured:
+                    params.structured_outputs = StructuredOutputsParams(
+                        json=STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_SCHEMA

+                sampling_params.append(params)
+                request_index += 1

+from dataclasses import replace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.input_batch import InputBatch, InputBuffers
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.utils import DraftTokensHandler
+
+
+def _input_batch(req_ids: list[str], structured: bool) -> InputBatch:
+    num_reqs = len(req_ids)
+    buffers = InputBuffers(num_reqs, num_reqs, torch.device("cuda"))
+    batch = InputBatch.make_dummy(num_reqs, num_reqs, buffers, is_padding=False)
+    return replace(batch, req_ids=req_ids, has_structured_output_reqs=structured)
+
+
+def _set_draft_toks(
+    handler: DraftTokensHandler,
+    req_ids: list[str],
+    tokens: list[list[int]],
+    structured: bool,
+) -> None:
+    batch = _input_batch(req_ids=req_ids, structured=structured)
+    handler.set_draft_tokens(batch, torch.tensor(tokens, device="cuda"))
+
+
+def _get_draft_toks(handler: DraftTokensHandler) -> dict[str, list[int]]:
+    drafts = handler.get_draft_tokens()
+    assert drafts is not None
+    return dict(zip(drafts.req_ids, drafts.draft_token_ids, strict=True))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="Requires CUDA")
+def test_draft_tokens_follow_request_lifecycle() -> None:
+    handler = DraftTokensHandler(torch.device("cuda"))
+
+    # The worker samples two structured-output requests
+    _set_draft_toks(
+        handler,
+        req_ids=["a", "b"],
+        tokens=[[11, 12], [21, 22]],
+        structured=True,
+    )
+
+    # "b" finishes before this result is handed back to the scheduler
+    handler.discard("b")
+    assert _get_draft_toks(handler) == {"a": [11, 12]}
+
+    # "a" continues and "b" is re-added with a new draft row
+    _set_draft_toks(
+        handler,
+        req_ids=["a", "b"],
+        tokens=[[13, 14], [23, 24]],
+        structured=True,
+    )
+    assert _get_draft_toks(handler) == {
+        "a": [13, 14],
+        "b": [23, 24],
+    }
+
+    # A batch without structured-output must not erase drafts from live requests
+    _set_draft_toks(
+        handler,
+        req_ids=["plain"],
+        tokens=[[31, 32]],
+        structured=False,
+    )
+    assert _get_draft_toks(handler) == {
+        "a": [13, 14],
+        "b": [23, 24],
+        "plain": [-1, -1],
+    }
+
+    # Requests finish independently, and the handler is empty once all are gone
+    handler.discard("a")
+    assert _get_draft_toks(handler) == {
+        "b": [23, 24],
+        "plain": [-1, -1],
+    }
+    handler.discard("b")
+    handler.discard("plain")
+    assert _get_draft_toks(handler) == {}

Wow! The perf recovery for PP2 is great!

Thanks for taking this on — and for the co-author credit. I reviewed the
rework end to end and independently reproduced your validation on our
hardware in hopes of saving others some time.

**Your regression diagnosis is correct, and the trace names the exact
mechanism.** Under PP + async, the single-slot payload's req_ids belong to the
*other* microbatch group, so the deferred fetch never fills the placeholders →
`num_acceptable = 0` → **every draft of every structured request is
force-rejected on every step** → acceptance length collapses to ~1. That
matches your E2E failure on main (0.0632 vs 0.0940) and the +211%/+440%
PP=2 recovery. In every reachable interleaving we traced — PP stagger, PP=1,
sync and async scheduling, preemption/resume, warmup,
first-decode-after-prefill, request-id reuse — the dict entry fetched for a
deferred batch is exactly the proposal that batch verifies. The pin is
structural: the RPC send order in `step_with_batch_queue` (exec →
pop+`result()` → `take_draft` → `sample`), sequential worker RPC processing,
and the `next_decode_eligible_step` stagger. Revert hygiene is complete: no
dangling consumers of `num_acceptable_drafts`, and the rejection sampler's
`-1`-padding semantics keep all-`-1` windows inert.

**Independent reproduction** (your branch @ `22b49f9007` = PR head):
scheduler + async_scheduler + structured_output + rejection_sampler_utils
suites: 577 passed, 1 xfailed. GPU worker suites (draft_tokens_handler,
batch_shard, sampler chunking/i64): 115 passed, 0 failed. Your three-way E2E,
one run each: main @ `6ee316eaea` fails on acceptance 0.0549 < 0.0940,
revert-only @ `048ae05ea1` fails on the identical `["blue", "` output, your
branch passes — consistent with your CI.

Two findings and three nits:

**1. The comparison your PR doesn't include — retention+masking vs
retention-only — measured on your gist runner** (`Qwen/Qwen3-4B` +
`RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark`, PP=2, K=8 async, broad/tight × c1/c96,
10 repeats per case): your branch @ `22b49f9007` vs our #61348 branch @
`67155a14dc` (retention *with* the #54442 masking still in place), two 96GB
GPUs (absolute numbers differ from your H100 table; the A/B is what matters;
runs were sequential, deltas straddle zero):

| case | retention-only tok/s | retention+masking tok/s | delta [95% CI on diff] |
|---|---|---|---|
| broad / c1 | 453.1 [±1.5] | 453.1 [±1.1] | +0.01% [−0.4, +0.4] |

Every delta is inside its 95% CI and the difference CIs straddle zero: the
masking costs nothing when vintage is correct. Mechanistically that's
expected — the first rejected draft sits at a real-mask row
(fill-before-inspect, `structured_output/__init__.py:476-502`), the
acceptance chain stops there, and the `_full_mask` rows are never sampled.
The revert deletes the fail-closed backstop for no measurable gain.

**2. After this PR, nothing detects vintage divergence at runtime.**
Relative to main, the PR reverts the only fail-closed backstop (#54442);
relative to #61348, it also declines the `check_draft_vintage` runtime check
in favor of the E2E repro. The E2E is `@multi_gpu_only(num_gpus=2)` (skipped
in most CI lanes) and asserts aggregate 5%-tolerance floors — it catches
gross collapse, not intermittent divergence; a stale-vintage window where
temp=0 output happens to be schema-valid passes both detectors. A future

fail-closed rationale and the handoff fix being the right fix for the race
are both settled in this thread, and I agree with both.

The handoff fix restores trust in drafts that the **race** corrupted. But
#54442 was fail-closed against a second source of untrusted drafts behind
a bitmask: **grammar-invalid proposals**. That path is independent of the
handoff and still exists on this branch:

1. The drafter proposes a token the grammar rejects → the scheduler's
   `validate_tokens` drops it and pads the window with `-1`
   (`spec_token_ids.extend([-1] * num_invalid_tokens)` in
   `update_draft_token_ids`).

2. `StructuredOutputManager`'s bitmask fill treats the first `-1` as
   `seen_padding`, and every later row is filled with
   `apply_bitmask=False` — all-permissive. The `failed_index` reuse only
   fires when a *real* token is rejected during the fill, which cannot
   happen once padding starts (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py`,
   the serial fill loop: `if token == -1: seen_padding = True`).

3. The worker then verifies its device-side proposals at those positions
   (`gpu_model_runner.py` draft-verify path + `rejection_sampler.py`), so
   the model samples from an unmasked row at a position it really does
   sample — the exact failure #54437 reported.

#54442's guard (`grammar_invalid_drafts`, deleted by this PR) was the
fail-closed mechanism for precisely this path; its deleted test
(`tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py`) states the contract in
the docstring:

> `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` fills row i before it inspects
> `req_tokens[i]`, so with the first -1 placeholder at index j rows 0..j
> carry a real mask and rows j+1.. carry the all-permissive `_full_mask`.
> Drafts j..K-1 must therefore be rejected, or the request samples with no
> grammar constraint at a position the model really does sample.

The E2E here is real but stochastic coverage: it passes because the DFlash
drafter's proposals in the test happen to be grammar-valid at the asserted
positions, not because the padded path is closed. A drafter that proposes
a grammar-invalid token under a constrained request would walk straight
through it.

Three ways to close it, in increasing invasiveness:

1. **Re-add `grammar_invalid_drafts`** scoped to the grammar-invalid path
   (the deleted test is CPU-only and passes on main — it can come back
   verbatim).
2. **Constrain the rows CPU-side**: when padding originates from
   `validate_tokens` invalidation, fill later rows from the last valid
   grammar state (the `failed_index` reuse already does this for
   fill-time rejections — the padding path just never sets it).
3. **Extend the E2E** with a drafter that deterministically proposes a
   grammar-invalid token, so the padded path is exercised on every run
   rather than by race timing.

Happy to put up (1) or (3) as a follow-up commit on this PR if you'd
rather not rework the handler — the deleted test is a working starting
point either way.

Michael, not sure I follow the "second source of untrusted drafts". Say the proposed drafts are `[valid, valid, invalid, ...]`, the position at `invalid` is still constrained. `invalid` will be rejected during rejection sampling and an alternative grammar-valid token will sampled. Bitmask positions beyond `invalid` are not used.

I've rebased and re-ran tests.

Confirmed — the fill fills row `j` before it inspects the `-1`, so the first invalid position is constrained, and reject-at-first-mismatch makes the rows beyond it unreachable. Withdrawing my concern; the handoff fix does cover it. Thanks for walking it back to the code.
Thanks Nick! I've re-validated with adjustments and they make sense to me.

## Overview

CI #98149 on PR #63219 (`12d9af7`) concluded with three failed lanes
and two distinct causes.

Cause 1 (fixture gap, fix offered): the two executor+worker lanes
(`nvidia-h200-mig-18gb-...-shard 2/2`, `amd-mi355-dpx-v1-executor-plus-worker`)
fail `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_streaming.py` with
`AttributeError: Mock object has no attribute 'draft_tokens_handler'`
(2 failed each; H200: 22 passed , AMD:
942 passed ). This is a test-fixture
gap (the mock predates the PR's new call sites), not a handler-logic
bug. One-line fixture fix, verified, pushed for cherry-picking.

Cause 2 (needs a baseline check before attributing):
`nvidia-l4-nightly-v1-e2e` fails the PR's own repro
`test_structured_output_pp.py[pp2-tp1]` with `EngineDeadError` — the
engine was killed by the GPU<->CPU sync guard:
`RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with
gpu_sync_allowed()`, raised on Worker_PP0 at 6/96 prompts
. The other two param variants
passed.

## Claims

- The two failing tests are `test_e2e_streaming_request_update_basic_flow`
  and `test_e2e_streaming_with_multimodal_features`; both bind the real
  `GPUModelRunner._remove_request` / `add_requests` onto
  `Mock(spec=GPUModelRunner)` and exercise them.
- Root cause: this PR adds `self.draft_tokens_handler.discard(req_id)` in
  `_remove_request` and `self.draft_tokens_handler.begin_step(...)`
  in `execute_model`. `draft_tokens_handler` is an instance attribute set
  in `__init__`, so it is not in `dir(GPUModelRunner)` and therefore not
  in the mock's spec — the first bound-method call hits the spec wall.
- `draft_tokens_handler` is the only instance attribute the bound
  `_remove_request` touches that the fixture does not already set (the
  method's `self.*` accesses: draft_tokens_handler, encoder_cache,
  lora_state, model_state, pooling_runner, pp_handler,
  prompt_logprobs_worker, req_states — all others are set in the fixture).
- The fix is one line in the fixture:
  `runner.draft_tokens_handler = Mock()`, matching the fixture's existing
  pattern for instance attributes the bound methods touch
  (`runner.model_state = Mock()`, `runner.lora_state = Mock()`, ...).
  With it: 2 passed. 
- L4 finding: the guard's firing frame is
  `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pp_utils.py:158` — `keep_t = torch.as_tensor(keep,
  device=self.device)` in `PPHandler.get_prev_sampled_outputs`, called
  from the worker's `execute_model` path. That code is pre-existing main
  and is not touched by this PR's diff. Whether the PR changes the
  trigger path (values or timing of `keep`) is unverified; the same test
  passed on H100/B200 runs without the guard, so the trigger is
  timing/config-dependent.

## Duplicate work check

- Searched the PR thread and open PRs for `draft_tokens_handler`,
  `test_gpu_model_runner_v2_streaming`, `streaming runner fixture`,
  `gpu_sync_allowed`; no comment or PR addresses either cause. The
  failing tests exist only on #63219's branch (first CI run on this PR
  was #98149).

## Validation

- Reproducer (before): `pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_streaming.py -q`
  at PR head `12d9af7` — 2 failed with the identical AttributeError. 
- Reproducer (after): same command with the one-line fix — 2 passed. 
- Fix pushed on top of the PR head on my fork, branch
  `pr-63219-ci-fix` — cherry-pick invited, or I can open it as a stacked
  PR if preferred.
- L4 evidence is the CI log itself (the guard's own error names the
  contract and the firing frame). No local repro: the failure needs a
  2-GPU PP lane with the sync guard enabled; GPU pool on our box is
  fully loaded.

## Details

- Mechanism: `Mock(spec=GPUModelRunner)` specs from `dir()` of the class
  object; attributes assigned in `__init__` are invisible to it. The
  fixture already handles this for every other instance attribute the
  bound methods touch — the PR simply introduced a new one after the
  fixture was written. The failure was latent since base commit
  `c67afdec`; #98149 is this PR's first CI run, which is why it surfaced
  now.
- Implication for upstream: none beyond this PR — no production code
  path is wrong; the runner's `draft_tokens_handler` exists on every real
  runner. The streaming tests' purpose (request-state streaming) is
  unchanged; the fix asserts nothing new about draft bookkeeping.
- Offered follow-up: none needed beyond the cherry-pick for cause 1.
  For cause 2, we suggest a baseline: `/ci retry` on this PR or a main-
  branch run of the L4 lane would show whether the guard trip predates
  the PR. Happy to help test either way.
- Note: even with the fixture fix cherry-picked, the L4 lane stays red
  until cause 2 is resolved (if it is PR-related) or the lane flakes
  clear (if it is not).

AI assistance was used for this diagnosis; the claims above are backed by
the reproduction commands and before/after logs referenced in Validation.
